1.explanation:
- lib/draw/SvgTransformUtil.js: The errors (“setTranslate on 'SVGTransform': The provided float value is non-finite”) originate here when trying to apply a NaN translation. We need to guard against NaN inputs.

- lib/draw/PathMap.js: This module computes SVG path data (bounding box, center) for grouped shapes. When the Group is empty (no children), its hit-box and center calculations produce undefined or NaN values.

- lib/features/modeling/behavior/GroupBehavior.js: This behavior handles creation and updating of Groups. It does not special-case an empty group’s geometry, so an empty group ends up with malformed bounds in the model.

- lib/features/auto-place/AutoPlaceUtil.js: The auto-placement utility uses the computed group bounds to suggest a drop location. Feeding it NaN bounds propagates invalid coordinates into the drag/drop routines.

Together, these files form the pipeline—from semantic/model updates (GroupBehavior), to geometry computation (PathMap), to placement hints (AutoPlaceUtil), down into SVG transforms (SvgTransformUtil)—and need coordinated fixes to properly initialize or guard empty-group bounds so no NaN values are ever passed to the renderer.
1.bug_scenario: When you start with an empty BPMN canvas (after deleting the default start event), add a Group container and then try to place any other element (e.g. a Pool), the editor throws repeated “provided float value is non-finite” errors (from SvgTransformUtil.setTranslate) and becomes unresponsive. In the attached gif you can see: 1) delete start event, 2) add a group, 3) drag a pool into the diagram, 4) console flood of NaN errors and stuck interaction. This happens because downstream placement and transform routines receive invalid (NaN) coordinates for the newly created, empty Group.

2.explanation:
All of the above files participate in the creation, sizing and drawing of the Group artifact, and a missing or undefined width/height (and missing DI bounds) for the new Group leads downstream to non-finite translate values when diagram-js attempts to drag or position the next shape:

• BpmnFactory.js
  – responsible for producing the semantic element and its initial shape attributes (width/height). Currently it does not supply default dimensions for “bpmn:Group,” so newly created groups have undefined size.

• BpmnUpdater.js
  – hooks into the generic AddShapeHandler to produce a DI entry for new BPMN elements. It does not create a bounds definition for groups, so element.di.bounds is undefined.

• BpmnRenderer.js
  – draws the outline of a Group by delegating to BpmnRenderUtil. Because size is undefined, it ends up calculating an invalid SVG path or invisible bounding box.

• BpmnRenderUtil.js
  – contains the path-construction logic for group shapes (getGroupPath). It takes in width/height (undefined) and emits NaN path commands. Later, when diagram-js tries to getBBox or apply setTranslate, it passes NaN and the browser throws the non-finite error.

Fixing this requires supplying a sensible default size (e.g. 100×80) and creating DI bounds when the user drops a new Group, so that BpmnRenderer and the diagram-js drag/translate logic always work with finite numbers.
2.bug_scenario: Starting from a completely empty diagram (only the default BPMN plane), the user deletes the start event and then adds a “Group” artifact. At that moment, the editor seems to accept the group, but immediately afterwards—on the very next create action (for example dragging in a Pool from the palette)—the diagram-js create/drag code throws “provided float value is non-finite” errors (originating in SvgTransformUtil.js). The pool (or any element) never actually lands on the canvas and the editor UI locks up in an unusable state.
